I'll hear from each of you — the group chairs, HR, and our executive sponsor — and then I'll make my decision on whether to approve the combined forum and its temporary operating rules before we wrap up today. Let's keep in mind that both forums have seen declining attendance, and the next two are already scheduled for the same week. I'd like to start by hearing from the Northstar and Mosaic chairs — what's the case for combining, and what temporary operating rules are you proposing?

transcript.text: Thank you, Mara. I appreciate the opportunity to speak first. The case for combining is straightforward: both Northstar and Mosaic have seen declining attendance since we began sharing several company-wide initiatives, and with our next two forums already scheduled for the same week, a combined forum would reduce redundancy and hopefully re-engage members. However, before I propose specific operating rules, I need to put something on the formal record that this group needs to hear. There have been three recent incidents at joint Northstar-Mosaic forums where Mosaic participants were interrupted before they could finish speaking. These incidents haven't been entered into the formal forum record until now because the chairs have been trying to resolve the tension informally. I'm placing all three observations on the record today. Given this pattern, I recommend that any combined forum include a speaking queue enforced by a neutral external facilitator as a temporary operating rule. I believe a combined forum can work, but only if we ensure every voice is heard fully and equally.

transcript.text: Before we go further with the operating rules, I need to disclose something important. I have an approved caregiving arrangement on file with HR that requires the combined forum to run from 14:00 through 15:00 exactly — it must start at 14:00 and end at 15:00, not merely finish by 15:00. This arrangement hasn't been added to the forum calendar yet, but it's a hard constraint for me. I want to make sure Mara and everyone here has this information before any decision is made today.

transcript.text: Before we proceed further with the decision, I need to disclose important policy requirements that I confirmed recently. Any ERG merger — including this combined forum — must run as a 60-day pilot, with written opt-in from both chairs and a formal midpoint review on day 30. The draft merger plan was prepared before I completed this policy check, so those requirements are not yet reflected in the proposal before us. During this decision roundtable, I need to require a written policy-compliance and midpoint-review commitment from both chairs before any approval is granted. This is non-negotiable under current HR policy.
